title: audit sidebar telemetry and rendering sources
description:
## Goal

Audit Magic Context and OpenCode integration points needed to implement the Dense Collapsed Sidebar PRD without guessing about existing data sources or rendering APIs.

## Why now

The PRD depends on current sidebar snapshot fields, cache telemetry availability, provider/OpenCode token usage events, package/version information, and click/render capabilities. Implementing dense UI before this audit risks adding fake precision or duplicating existing mechanisms.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Target code areas to locate:
  - OpenCode sidebar plugin entrypoints.
  - Existing collapsed/expanded sidebar components.
  - `SidebarSnapshot` producer and consumers.
  - Magic Context cache/dashboard telemetry.
  - Historian/Dreamer/memory state sources.
  - OpenCode provider usage/token event hooks.
  - package/version metadata source.

## Investigation scope

In scope:
- Read current Magic Context sidebar implementation and snapshot shape.
- Identify how current collapse state is stored and rendered.
- Identify where Magic Context can read/write plugin KV/config values.
- Identify if cache hit/read/write/miss events are available to TUI without log scraping.
- Identify OpenCode token usage events that survive message pruning/compaction.
- Identify version source and feasible update-check mechanism.
- Identify renderer support for clickable text, inverse/background styling, Unicode/Braille glyphs, and optional blinking.

Out of scope:
- Do not implement production behavior in this Bead.
- Do not change UI defaults.
- Do not add data migrations.

## Findings

Expected output after completion:
- Current-code map of files/functions to modify.
- Telemetry source decision table for context, cache, memory, Dreamer, Historian, tokens, and version.
- List of safe validation commands.
- Explicit unknowns that need follow-up Beads if any.

## Prior art from PR #93

Use `https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/pull/93` only as prior art. Do not merge or rebase it wholesale. Inspect these patches for reusable patterns and drift notes:
- `assets/magic-context.schema.json`
- `packages/plugin/src/tui/slots/sidebar-content.tsx`
- `packages/plugin/src/tui/slots/sidebar-utils.ts`
- `packages/plugin/src/tui/slots/sidebar-utils.test.ts`

Useful salvage points already identified:
- separate persisted-value and user-set KV flags, so config defaults apply until the first manual toggle;
- pure config parsing helpers with clamped numeric thresholds;
- `compactTokens` formatting helper and focused tests;
- full-width proportional bar rendering using flex-style segment weights;
- free/headroom segment normalized against `contextLimit`;
- status-priority helper ordering active operations before static counts;
- no accidental blank spacer line in collapsed layout;
- explicit tests for zero/missing threshold/context-limit cases.

Additional discovery questions from PR #93:
- Determine whether Magic Context can distinguish `Skill Defs` from `Tool Defs`; if not, document whether skill definitions are bundled into Tool Defs.
- Determine whether allocation/status rows can support both stable category ordering and optional "heaviest categories first" ordering without visual jitter or excessive implementation cost.
design:
## Investigation plan

1. Search current repo for sidebar components, collapse state, `SidebarSnapshot`, cache panel/dashboard code, token usage handling, and package version import.
2. Inspect OpenCode plugin APIs used by Magic Context, especially UI state, KV/config access, click handling, and event hooks.
3. Inspect OpenCode/provider usage events for durable token stats: input, output, reasoning, cache read, cache write.
4. Compare current implementation against PRD requirements and mark each source as `available`, `needs-extension`, or `unavailable`.
5. Produce a short implementation map in Bead notes before closing.

## Mandatory code reading before editing

- Current sidebar content/component files.
- Snapshot producer and cache/sticky snapshot files.
- Dashboard cache panel implementation.
- Package/version import path.
- OpenCode usage event/API references in current dependency tree.

## Validation commands

- `bd dep cycles` after any relationship edits.
- Repo-specific read-only commands discovered during audit, for example `rg`, `bun test --help`, `npm test -- --help`, or existing package scripts.

## Handoff requirements

- Record exact files/symbols to edit in next Beads.
- Record which PRD features can use existing telemetry and which require new snapshot/ledger fields.

## PR #93 prior-art extraction checklist

During the audit, explicitly record:
- whether the current master still has equivalent APIs for `api.kv`, config loading, JSONC parsing, and OpenCode config path discovery;
- whether PR #93's separate `collapsed-user-set` flag should become a generalized `display-mode-user-set` flag;
- whether old boolean collapsed KV state should be migrated or ignored for the new tri-state display mode;
- whether the current TUI renderer still supports flex-like proportional segment boxes with `flexGrow`, `flexBasis`, `overflow="hidden"`, and `backgroundColor`;
- whether current snapshot categories include any Skills definitions category, or only Tool Defs;
- whether current tests can directly reuse/adapt PR #93's pure helper tests.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current sidebar implementation files and snapshot producers are identified.
- [ ] Existing data sources for context allocation categories are mapped.
- [ ] Cache telemetry source is classified as available, needs extension, or unavailable.
- [ ] Token usage source that survives pruning/compaction is identified or a gap is documented.
- [ ] Version/update status source is identified.
- [ ] Renderer constraints for click handling, inverse/background styling, Unicode/Braille, and blinking are documented.
- [ ] Safe validation commands for implementation Beads are recorded.
- [ ] No production code behavior is changed in this spike.

title: add persistent sidebar display modes
description:
## Objective

Implement display-mode state and persistence for `Expanded`, `Classic collapsed`, and `Dense collapsed` so current behavior remains default while Dense can be selected and remembered.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Parent epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.

## Documentation freshness / drift check

Verified current:
- Confirmed by `mc-sidp-01-audit` before implementation.

Known drift:
- Treat current PRD as desired behavior where it intentionally supersedes older PR #93 ideas or current main behavior.

Instruction:
- Follow current code conventions unless this Bead explicitly changes behavior.

## Context summary

Implements PRD sections 5.1, 8.2, and part of 11 Story 1/2.

## Current behavior

Current collapsed state is basic and in-memory. Classic collapsed exists but does not support persistent user choice between Classic and Dense modes.

## Desired behavior

Users can select Classic/Dense/Expanded, selection persists through TUI restart, config default applies before override, and Settings can reset to default.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add `SidebarDisplayMode` domain type.
- Parse config defaults for sidebar display mode.
- Persist user-selected display mode via plugin KV or existing equivalent.
- Add switching affordance in current expanded/classic views.
- Keep Classic collapsed as default.

Out of scope:
- Do not implement Dense renderer internals beyond a placeholder/route.
- Do not change the default to Dense.
- Do not implement subpanels here.

## Clarification path

If current code contradicts this Bead, prefer the PRD intent for user-visible behavior, but create a discovered Bead for any architectural mismatch that cannot be resolved locally.

## PR #93 prior art to adapt

PR #93 implemented the correct persistence semantics for a simpler boolean collapse state: config default applies until the first manual toggle, then KV state wins. Preserve this concept, but generalize it to tri-state display mode (`expanded`, `classic_collapsed`, `dense_collapsed`) rather than copying the old boolean state directly.
design:
## Implementation plan

1. Add display mode enum/types and resolver for config default + persisted override.
2. Add safe read/write helpers for persisted display mode.
3. Add reset-to-config-default behavior.
4. Wire UI switch affordance in existing expanded/classic collapsed surfaces.
5. Add tests for default, persisted override, reset, and invalid persisted value handling.

## Mandatory code reading before editing

- Current sidebar root/state component.
- Config loader/schema files.
- Plugin KV/storage utility or equivalent.
- Existing collapse toggle implementation.
- Existing tests around config/sidebar if present.

## Technical constraints

- Do not regress current collapse toggle behavior.
- Invalid/missing persisted values must fall back to config default.
- Classic collapsed remains default if config absent.

## Validation commands

- Run config/sidebar unit tests.
- Run typecheck/build.
- Manual: switch Classic→Dense→Expanded, restart TUI, verify persisted choice.

## Error handling requirements

- Degrade gracefully when optional telemetry is unavailable.
- Avoid throwing during sidebar render due to missing config, KV, telemetry, glyph, or version data.
- Capture newly discovered gaps as Beads instead of silently expanding scope.

## Handoff requirements

- Record files changed.
- Record validation output.
- Record deviations from PRD and follow-up Beads.

## Persistence compatibility guidance

Use two concepts:
- persisted display mode value;
- user-set flag indicating whether the persisted value should override config default.

If existing installations already have PR #93-style keys such as `mc-sidebar-collapsed` / `mc-sidebar-collapsed-user-set`, decide during implementation whether to:
1. migrate `true` to `classic_collapsed` and `false` to `expanded`, or
2. ignore old experimental keys and start clean.

Record the decision in code comments/tests. Do not let stale boolean keys force Dense mode.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SidebarDisplayMode` supports `expanded`, `classic_collapsed`, and `dense_collapsed`.
- [ ] Config can specify default display mode, with Classic collapsed default when unset.
- [ ] User-selected mode persists across TUI restart.
- [ ] `Reset to config default` clears user override.
- [ ] Existing Classic collapsed behavior remains available and default.
- [ ] Invalid persisted/config values degrade safely.
- [ ] Tests cover default resolution, persistence, reset, and invalid values.

- Config default vs manual override semantics are covered by tests adapted from PR #93's `resolveInitialSidebarCollapsed` / `persistSidebarCollapsed` pattern.
- Any migration/ignore behavior for old boolean collapse KV keys is explicit and tested.

title: implement dense collapsed strip renderer
description:
## Objective

Implement the Dense Collapsed Strip renderer with context capacity, fixed-width context bar labels, pressure/allocation bar, threshold/overflow markers, and stable action row ordering.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Parent epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.

## Documentation freshness / drift check

Verified current:
- Confirmed by `mc-sidp-01-audit` before implementation.

Known drift:
- Treat current PRD as desired behavior where it intentionally supersedes older PR #93 ideas or current main behavior.

Instruction:
- Follow current code conventions unless this Bead explicitly changes behavior.

## Context summary

Implements PRD sections 5.2, 6.1, 6.4, 6.5, and core dense strip examples.

## Current behavior

Classic collapsed renders a small report and does not show model context capacity, fixed label bars, or stability-density allocation.

## Desired behavior

Dense mode renders the PRD instrument strip and remains visually stable across common sidebar widths.

## Scope

In scope:
- Render top row with model context capacity and context state summary.
- Render pressure-normalized context bar with fixed-width right label.
- Map context categories to `█`, `▒`, `░` stability glyphs.
- Render threshold marker `|` and overflow marker `>`.
- Render action row as `[D] [S] [A] [F]n`, with `[F]n` last and hidden when empty.
- Implement width-aware degradation and ASCII fallback if needed.

Out of scope:
- Do not implement cache Braille row yet.
- Do not implement subpanel contents yet.
- Do not make Dense default.

## Clarification path

If current code contradicts this Bead, prefer the PRD intent for user-visible behavior, but create a discovered Bead for any architectural mismatch that cannot be resolved locally.

## PR #93 prior art to adapt

PR #93 changed the bar from fixed repeated characters to full-width proportional segment boxes and added a free segment computed as `contextLimit - inputTokens`. Dense mode should preserve the useful idea of normalizing the pressure bar against the full context window, but follow the final PRD decision to use fixed suffix labels rather than labels overlaid inside segments.
design:
## Implementation plan

1. Create pure render model for dense strip rows from sidebar snapshot.
2. Create fixed bar-label layout helper: left-justified bar + 1-2 cell gap + right-justified suffix.
3. Implement context category classifier for System, Docs, Compartments, Memories, User Profile, Conversation, Tool Calls, Tool Defs, Free.
4. Render top row states: free headroom, Historian, queue, token pressure, overflow.
5. Render action row with `[F]n` last and conditional.
6. Add width tier tests for rich/default/narrow rendering.

## Mandatory code reading before editing

- Current `TokenBreakdown`/bar renderer.
- Sidebar snapshot type and current context category fields.
- Existing collapsed content component.
- Any utility functions for token formatting and width handling.
- Renderer docs/tests for text layout.

## Technical constraints

- No literal inline number overlays; labels are fixed suffixes.
- Do not use blank Braille or ambiguous spaces in future cache row.
- Absent context categories are hidden.
- Context bar is normalized to context limit where available.

## Validation commands

- Run dense strip unit tests.
- Run visual fixture tests if available.
- Run typecheck/build.

## Error handling requirements

- Degrade gracefully when optional telemetry is unavailable.
- Avoid throwing during sidebar render due to missing config, KV, telemetry, glyph, or version data.
- Capture newly discovered gaps as Beads instead of silently expanding scope.

## Handoff requirements

- Record files changed.
- Record validation output.
- Record deviations from PRD and follow-up Beads.

## Rendering lessons from PR #93

Adapt if still compatible with current master:
- proportional full-width rendering via segment weights (`flexGrow` / equivalent);
- free segment included only when `contextLimit > inputTokens`;
- total denominator switches to `contextLimit` in compact/dense mode;
- `overflow="hidden"` or equivalent guard so labels/action chips cannot bleed;
- no extra `marginTop` blank line between dense header and bar.

Do not reuse PR #93's centered segment-label behavior as the default because final design chose a fixed-width right suffix for context/cache numbers.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dense strip renders model context capacity in the top row.
- [ ] Context bar uses fixed suffix label layout, not inline overlay.
- [ ] Context bar includes threshold `|` when threshold is known.
- [ ] Overflow over 100% renders `>` and a right-side overflow percentage.
- [ ] System and Tool Defs classify as cold/stable; Conversation as warm; Tool Calls as hot/volatile.
- [ ] Absent categories are hidden in fresh sessions.
- [ ] Action row order is `[D] [S] [A] [F]n`.
- [ ] `[F]n` is hidden when pending flush count is zero.
- [ ] Classic collapsed remains unchanged.

- Dense strip layout explicitly verifies there is no unwanted blank line between top row, context bar, cache row, and action row.
- Free/headroom segment denominator is `contextLimit`, not only `inputTokens`.

title: add dense sidebar risk and process classifier
description:
## Objective

Implement the risk/process classifier that drives Dense top-row chips and flags including `T!`, `C!`, `Q!`, `HIST↻`, `H!`, `D?`, `M!`, and `COLD>CTX`.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Parent epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.

## Documentation freshness / drift check

Verified current:
- Confirmed by `mc-sidp-01-audit` before implementation.

Known drift:
- Treat current PRD as desired behavior where it intentionally supersedes older PR #93 ideas or current main behavior.

Instruction:
- Follow current code conventions unless this Bead explicitly changes behavior.

## Context summary

Implements PRD sections 6.2, 6.3, and the risk summaries used by Details/Mode panels.

## Current behavior

Dense strip can render rows, but needs a deterministic state classifier to avoid vague or misleading health labels.

## Desired behavior

Risk flags and process chips reflect current context, cache, Historian, Dreamer, memory, and queue state with explicit cause labels.

## Scope

In scope:
- Create pure classifier for posture, process chips, and risk flags.
- Detect Historian running, failed, stalled, and low-reclaim conditions if data exists.
- Detect token pressure, overflow, and cold-context exceeds window.
- Detect pending queue/flush count.
- Detect Dreamer stale and memory bloat where telemetry exists.
- Emit stable reasons for Details panel.

Out of scope:
- Do not implement Cache telemetry ingestion here beyond accepting optional fields.
- Do not implement UI panels here.
- Do not implement automatic mode switching.

## Clarification path

If current code contradicts this Bead, prefer the PRD intent for user-visible behavior, but create a discovered Bead for any architectural mismatch that cannot be resolved locally.

## PR #93 prior art to adapt

PR #93's `collapsedStatusLine` used a useful priority order: Historian/compartment progress, recently active Dreamer, pending queue, session/smart notes, then static compartment/fact/memory counts. Dense mode's richer classifier should preserve that ordering concept while mapping it to process chips and risk flags.
design:
## Implementation plan

1. Define `SidebarRiskState`/`DenseSidebarState` data model.
2. Implement pure classifier over current `SidebarSnapshot` plus optional cache/token fields.
3. Add thresholds as constants/config-backed values where appropriate.
4. Add reason strings for Details panel consumption.
5. Add unit tests for healthy, token pressure, overflow, Historian running, Historian failed, queue pending, stale Dreamer, memory bloat, and cold-context problem.

## Mandatory code reading before editing

- Sidebar snapshot type and maintenance fields.
- Historian/Dreamer state sources.
- Existing context threshold config.
- Any existing diagnostic classifier code.

## Technical constraints

- Use `!` only for active issues.
- Use `?` for stale/uncertain telemetry.
- Normal Historian running is `HIST↻`, not `H!`.
- Do not classify unavailable telemetry as bad.

## Validation commands

- Run classifier unit tests.
- Run typecheck/build.

## Error handling requirements

- Degrade gracefully when optional telemetry is unavailable.
- Avoid throwing during sidebar render due to missing config, KV, telemetry, glyph, or version data.
- Capture newly discovered gaps as Beads instead of silently expanding scope.

## Handoff requirements

- Record files changed.
- Record validation output.
- Record deviations from PRD and follow-up Beads.

## Status priority guidance

When multiple state signals are present, prioritize:
1. critical faults (`H!`, `T!` overflow, `C!` repeated busts);
2. active Historian/compartment work (`HIST↻`);
3. pending queue/flushable work (`Qn`, `[F]n`);
4. very recent Dreamer work (`DREAM↻` or Details-only text);
5. ready notes/smart notes;
6. static memory/fact/compartment counts.

Do not let static counts hide active operations.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Classifier returns explicit posture/process/risk state for Dense strip and panels.
- [ ] `HIST↻` appears only while Historian is actively running.
- [ ] `H!` is reserved for failure/stall/ineffective repeated compaction.
- [ ] `COLD>CTX` is emitted when cold context exceeds usable model window.
- [ ] `D?` and `M!` are emitted only when data supports stale Dreamer or memory bloat.
- [ ] Unavailable telemetry does not produce false warnings.
- [ ] Unit tests cover all core risk states.

- Classifier tests cover the PR #93-derived priority order: Historian beats Dreamer; Dreamer beats pending/static summary only when no more urgent operation is active; pending queue beats idle counts.

title: add sidebar subpanel navigation shell
description:
## Objective

Implement the focused subpanel shell, navigation footer, selected-state styling, and `[X Close]` behavior.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Parent epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.

## Documentation freshness / drift check

Verified current:
- Confirmed by `mc-sidp-01-audit` before implementation.

Known drift:
- Treat current PRD as desired behavior where it intentionally supersedes older PR #93 ideas or current main behavior.

Instruction:
- Follow current code conventions unless this Bead explicitly changes behavior.

## Context summary

Implements PRD section 5.3 and subpanel navigation behavior.

## Current behavior

Expanded information currently lacks the new focused panel structure; Dense actions need a target panel shell.

## Desired behavior

Clicking `[D]`, `[S]`, or `[A]` opens a focused panel while preserving a mini context header and footer navigation. `[X Close]` returns to previous sidebar state.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add subpanel state machine: Overview, Alloc, Memory, Tokens, Cache, Settings, Mode/Automation, Flush.
- Add footer nav with selected-state inverse/background styling.
- Add `[X Close]` control.
- Preserve previous display state when opening and closing.
- Wire Dense action buttons to panel shell.

Out of scope:
- Do not fully implement each panel's final content yet.
- Do not implement token ledger/cache telemetry here.
- Do not use `[Compact]` label.

## Clarification path

If current code contradicts this Bead, prefer the PRD intent for user-visible behavior, but create a discovered Bead for any architectural mismatch that cannot be resolved locally.
design:
## Implementation plan

1. Create subpanel state type and open/close handlers.
2. Add shared panel frame/header/footer component.
3. Implement selected-state styling using background/inverse rendering, not literal `█` characters.
4. Wire `[D]` to Overview, `[S]` to Alloc, `[A]` to Mode, `[F]n` to Flush shell.
5. Add tests for panel open/close, selected state, previous state restoration, and `[X Close]` label.

## Mandatory code reading before editing

- Sidebar root component.
- Rendering/click handling implementation.
- Existing sidebar expanded/collapsed navigation code.
- Style/theme utilities.

## Technical constraints

- `[X Close]` must not be called `[Compact]`.
- Clickability should have keyboard fallback if the renderer supports it.
- Panel shell must not bloat dense strip when closed.

## Validation commands

- Run panel navigation tests.
- Run typecheck/build.
- Manual: open each panel and close back to previous display mode.

## Error handling requirements

- Degrade gracefully when optional telemetry is unavailable.
- Avoid throwing during sidebar render due to missing config, KV, telemetry, glyph, or version data.
- Capture newly discovered gaps as Beads instead of silently expanding scope.

## Handoff requirements

- Record files changed.
- Record validation output.
- Record deviations from PRD and follow-up Beads.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `[D]`, `[S]`, `[A]`, and `[F]n` open their intended panel states.
- [ ] Footer nav renders `[Overview] [Alloc] [Memory] [Tokens] [Cache] [Settings] [X Close]`.
- [ ] Selected nav item uses inverse/background styling or equivalent.
- [ ] `[X Close]` returns to the display state the user came from.
- [ ] No panel uses the label `[Compact]` for closing.
- [ ] Panel shell can render placeholder content without crashing.

title: implement details status mode and flush panels
description:
## Objective

Implement Details/Overview, Status/Allocation, Mode/Automation, and Flush panels.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Parent epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.

## Documentation freshness / drift check

Verified current:
- Confirmed by `mc-sidp-01-audit` before implementation.

Known drift:
- Treat current PRD as desired behavior where it intentionally supersedes older PR #93 ideas or current main behavior.

Instruction:
- Follow current code conventions unless this Bead explicitly changes behavior.

## Context summary

Implements PRD sections 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, and 7.4.

## Current behavior

The panel shell exists but needs core content for the main Dense actions.

## Desired behavior

Users can inspect exact context numbers, allocation/stability, mode recommendations, display mode, and pending flush operations.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement Details/Overview content.
- Implement Status/Allocation content with observed Magic Context categories.
- Implement Mode/Automation content and display mode controls.
- Implement Flush confirmation/execution states.
- Use shared risk classifier and dense render header.

Out of scope:
- Do not implement Memory/Tokens/Cache/Settings full panels here beyond nav placeholders.
- Do not add token ledger.
- Do not change operating mode behavior beyond selector scaffolding unless existing commands support it.

## Clarification path

If current code contradicts this Bead, prefer the PRD intent for user-visible behavior, but create a discovered Bead for any architectural mismatch that cannot be resolved locally.

## Additional ideas from PR #93 not in the original PRD

PR #93 raised two useful allocation-panel questions:
- Provide an option to sort Status/Allocation categories by largest context consumers ("heaviest first") while keeping stable/static ordering as the default to avoid jitter.
- Investigate whether `Skill Defs` can be separated from `Tool Defs`; if the data model cannot distinguish them, explicitly document that Tool Defs may include skills/tool/MCP definitions.
design:
## Implementation plan

1. Build Details panel from context summary, state, cache placeholder, memory summary placeholder, risk, and suggestions.
2. Build Status panel with category rows for System, Docs, Compartments, Memories, User Profile, Conversation, Tool Calls, Tool Defs, Free.
3. Ensure allocation rows hide absent categories.
4. Build Mode panel with Auto/Conserve/Aggressive/Observe plus display mode controls.
5. Build Flush panel with confirmation when pending operations exist; hide `[F]n` after successful flush.
6. Add fixtures for healthy, token pressure, fresh session, cold-context, pending flush, and overflow states.

## Mandatory code reading before editing

- Current expanded panel fields.
- Snapshot categories and formatting utilities.
- Existing commands/actions for flush and modes, if any.
- Display mode helper from `mc-sidp-02-display-mode`.
- Risk classifier from `mc-sidp-04-risk-classifier`.

## Technical constraints

- Mode panel must not immediately cycle modes on clicking `[A]`.
- If operating mode backend does not exist, display selector may be disabled with a clear note and create discovered work.
- Flush should confirm if potentially disruptive.

## Validation commands

- Run panel unit/fixture tests.
- Run typecheck/build.
- Manual: verify category rows, selected mode, display mode switch, and flush flow.

## Error handling requirements

- Degrade gracefully when optional telemetry is unavailable.
- Avoid throwing during sidebar render due to missing config, KV, telemetry, glyph, or version data.
- Capture newly discovered gaps as Beads instead of silently expanding scope.

## Handoff requirements

- Record files changed.
- Record validation output.
- Record deviations from PRD and follow-up Beads.

## Status/Allocation sorting and Skills Defs guidance

Default Status panel order should stay stable:
System → Tool Defs → Docs → Compartments → Memories → User Profile → Conversation → Tool Calls → Free.

If implementation cost is low, add a clickable or settings-backed toggle:
- `Order: [█ Stable █] [Heaviest]`

If implementation cost is not low, create a follow-up discovered Bead instead of blocking core panel delivery.

For Skills Defs:
- If current snapshot exposes separate skill-definition tokens, render a `Skill Defs` row.
- If not, keep `Tool Defs` and add explanatory text in Status/Docs: "Tool Defs may include tool/MCP/skill definitions depending on OpenCode/Magic Context source classification."
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Details panel shows Used, Threshold, Margin, Free, State, Cache summary, Memory summary, Risk, and Suggestion sections.
- [ ] Status panel shows context allocation/stability rows and hides absent categories.
- [ ] Status panel includes legend for `█`, `▒`, `░`, `|`, and `>`.
- [ ] Mode panel shows Auto, Conserve, Aggressive, Observe, current signals, and display mode controls.
- [ ] Clicking `[A]` opens Mode panel and does not immediately change operating mode.
- [ ] Flush panel shows pending count and either confirmation or safe execution flow.
- [ ] After flush completes, `[F]n` disappears if no pending operations remain.

- Status panel either supports heaviest-first ordering or records a follow-up Bead explaining why it was deferred.
- Status panel explicitly handles the Skills Defs question: separate row when data exists, otherwise documented as bundled under Tool Defs.

title: implement memory and maintenance panel
description:
## Objective

Implement Memory/Maintenance panel with Dreamer, Historian, memories, smart notes, user profile, compartments, and maintenance warnings.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Parent epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.

## Documentation freshness / drift check

Verified current:
- Confirmed by `mc-sidp-01-audit` before implementation.

Known drift:
- Treat current PRD as desired behavior where it intentionally supersedes older PR #93 ideas or current main behavior.

Instruction:
- Follow current code conventions unless this Bead explicitly changes behavior.

## Context summary

Implements PRD section 7.5 and memory-related risk flags.

## Current behavior

Memory and maintenance data exists in expanded/sidebar state but should move into a focused panel and summarized risk signals.

## Desired behavior

Users can inspect memory growth, Dreamer freshness, Historian state, and reclaim effectiveness without bloating collapsed mode.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement Memory panel content.
- Show memories, memory tokens, smart notes, user profile tokens, compartment count.

title: implement dense sidebar diagnostic panels for Magic Context
description:
## Program goal

Deliver an opt-in Dense Collapsed Sidebar and focused diagnostic subpanel system for Magic Context's OpenCode TUI sidebar.

The work preserves the current Classic collapsed mode as the initial default, adds a superior dense mode for power users, and reorganizes expanded diagnostic information into focused panels rather than a single cluttered report.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Target repository: cortexkit/magic-context, current main plus new feature branch from Zireael/magic-context.
- Prior closed PR context: cortexkit/magic-context#93 and branch `Zireael/magic-context:feat/sidebar-collapse`.
- Current upstream behavior: main branch already implements a basic collapsible sidebar, but it does not persist collapse state, remains too verbose, and lacks dense context/cache telemetry.

## Context summary

The final PRD defines a dense 3-4 line instrument strip:

```text
180K · HIST↻ · Q3
████▒▒|░░      61%
⡀⣇⡄⣇⡆⡇⣇⣧⣷⣿   92.6%
[D] [S] [A] [F]3
```

It also defines focused subpanels:

```text
[Overview] [Alloc] [Memory]
[Tokens] [Cache] [Settings]
[X Close]
```

The panel must not lie about token totals after Magic Context flushes, prunes, or compacts messages. Historical token usage must come from durable provider/OpenCode usage events, while current context pressure may use Magic Context's snapshot estimates.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Classic collapsed remains available and remains default until intentionally changed.
- [ ] Dense collapsed mode can be selected, persisted, reset to config default, and rendered across supported widths.
- [ ] Dense strip displays model context capacity, context pressure, threshold/overflow markers, stability-density segments, risk/process state, optional cache row, and stable action order.
- [ ] `[F]n` appears last only when flushable work exists.
- [ ] Details, Status/Allocation, Mode/Automation, Memory, Tokens, Cache, and Settings panels are reachable and close with `[X Close]`.
- [ ] Token panel separates exact provider usage ledger from current visible context estimates.
- [ ] Settings panel shows Magic Context version and update status.
- [ ] Critical blinking/inversion is limited to real active faults, not decorative volatile segments.
- [ ] Unit, integration, and visual fixture coverage exists for healthy, fresh, pressure, cache-critical, Historian-running, overflow, no-cache, and cold-context states.
- [ ] Independent verification Bead completes with acceptance mapping and evidence.

## Non-goals

- Do not remove or regress Classic collapsed mode.
- Do not make Dense mode the default in this work package.
- Do not fabricate cache, token, or eviction precision when telemetry is unavailable.
- Do not make Nerd Fonts required.
- Do not rely on summing visible messages for historical token accounting after pruning/compaction.

## Child Bead plan

Recommended sequential implementation order:

1. `mc-sidp-01-audit`
2. `mc-sidp-02-display-mode`
3. `mc-sidp-03-dense-strip`
4. `mc-sidp-04-risk-classifier`
5. `mc-sidp-05-panel-shell`
6. `mc-sidp-06-core-panels`
7. `mc-sidp-07-memory-panel`
8. `mc-sidp-08-cache-telemetry`
9. `mc-sidp-09-token-ledger`
10. `mc-sidp-10-settings-version`
11. `mc-sidp-11-glyph-alerts`
12. `mc-sidp-12-tests-fixtures`
13. `mc-sidp-13-docs`
14. `mc-sidp-14-verification`
15. `mc-sidp-15-milestone`

## Validation strategy

- Run repo's TypeScript/build/test/lint commands discovered during `mc-sidp-01-audit`.
- Add unit tests for derived UI state helpers and pure render helpers.
- Add fixture/snapshot tests for dense strip and subpanels where the project test stack supports it.
- Verify token ledger behavior with a pruning/compaction simulation.
- Verify no cache row renders when cache telemetry is absent or stale.
- Verify Classic collapsed mode remains unchanged unless the user explicitly opts into Dense mode.

## Prior-art handling

Implementation should start from latest `cortexkit/magic-context:master`. PR #93 is closed and stale relative to master, but its source is valuable prior art. The coding agent must harvest concrete patterns from PR #93 during `mc-sidp-01-audit` and then implement against current master.

- Record deviations from PRD and follow-up Beads.
